claims.text: Retention or loss of toughness in HEAs is governed by the interplay between lattice distortion and nanoscale precipitate formation.
Lattice distortion and nanoscale precipitates influence dislocation motion.
Lattice distortion and nanoscale precipitates influence resistance to crack propagation.
The initial HEA is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Heat treatment at 600°C for 24 hours will introduce controlled nanoscale precipitates.
Using an inert atmosphere during heat treatment will avoid oxidation.
Nanoscale precipitates act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Barrier action by nanoscale precipitates enhances toughness by impeding crack propagation.
Excessive precipitate formation may reduce ductility and cause embrittlement.
Precipitate coarsening may reduce ductility and cause embrittlement.
Relative to the untreated alloy, toughness will increase as precipitates are introduced until an optimal precipitate density is reached.
Beyond the optimal precipitate density, toughness will decrease because of embrittlement.
The experimental baseline is the toughness of the untreated alloy in its as-cast state.
The proposed behavior is expected to hold for HEAs that initially have a single-phase solid-solution structure.
The proposed behavior requires a composition that permits controlled precipitation without broader phase separation.
The heat-treatment temperature and duration that optimize precipitate formation vary with alloy composition.

A lack of toughness increase after introducing nanoscale precipitates, or a uniform toughness decrease independent of precipitate density, would falsify the proposed precipitate-mediated toughening behavior.

contradictions.description: The intervention requires precipitate formation, which ordinarily entails development of a compositionally or structurally distinct phase, while the boundary requires precipitate formation 'without phase separation.' This may be reconcilable for coherent clusters or a narrowly defined absence of macroscopic phase separation, but that distinction is not stated.
